title: New Study Finds Hidden Toxic Chemicals in Everyday Personal Care Products
subtitle: Most shampoos, lotions, and soaps contain substances not listed on their labels, raising serious health concerns for consumers.

summary.en: A recent study has revealed that a large majority of personal care products contain hidden toxic chemicals. Researchers tested over 110 common items and found that many included ingredients linked to cancer and other health problems. Even products labeled as natural or eco-friendly were found to contain dangerous compounds. The study highlights a major gap in current safety regulations for everyday goods. Experts are now calling for stricter oversight and mandatory testing to protect public health.
summary.zh: 一項近期研究揭露，絕大多數的個人護理產品含有隱藏的毒性化學物質。研究人員測試了超過一百一十種常見商品，發現許多產品含有與癌症及其他健康問題相關的成分。即使是標榜天然或環保的產品，也被發現含有危險化合物。這項研究凸顯了現行日常用品安全法規的重大漏洞。專家目前正呼籲加強監管並實施強制性檢測，以保護公眾健康。

paragraphs.en: A new investigation has brought fresh attention to the safety of everyday personal care products. Following up on recent reports about hidden dangers in household items, a new peer-reviewed study has confirmed that many common goods contain toxic chemicals that do not appear on their ingredient labels. This discovery has caused alarm among researchers and consumers alike, as it suggests that the products we use on our bodies every day may not be as safe as we believe.
paragraphs.zh: 一項新的調查讓大眾重新關注起日常個人護理產品的安全性。繼近期關於居家用品隱藏危險的報導後，一項經過同儕審查的最新研究證實，許多常見商品含有毒化學物質，但這些成分並未出現在產品標籤上。這項發現引起了研究人員與消費者的擔憂，因為這顯示我們每天塗抹在身上的產品，可能並不如我們所認為的那樣安全。

paragraphs.en: According to The Guardian Health, researchers tested more than 110 different items, including shampoos, baby lotions, soaps, and toothpaste. These products were purchased from major retailers like Target and Amazon. The results were concerning: about 85% of the tested items contained chemicals that were not listed on the packaging. On average, the products contained more than three times as many chemicals as the labels claimed.
paragraphs.zh: 根據《衛報健康版 (The Guardian Health)》報導，研究人員測試了超過一百一十種不同的商品，包括洗髮精、嬰兒乳液、肥皂與牙膏。這些產品購自目標百貨 (Target) 與亞馬遜 (Amazon) 等大型零售商。結果令人擔憂：約百分之八十五的受測商品含有未列在包裝上的化學物質。平均而言，這些產品所含的化學物質數量是標籤宣稱的三倍以上。

paragraphs.en: Jenna Hua, a lead author of the study from the company Million Marker, expressed her frustration with the findings. "I spend my money, and I want to get a good product – why am I being lied to?" she asked. The study identified several dangerous substances, including hormone disruptors and carcinogens — which are substances known to cause cancer. Other detected chemicals were linked to neurological diseases and reproductive harm. These substances can be absorbed into the body through the skin, making their presence in daily-use products a significant health concern.
paragraphs.zh: 該研究的主要作者、來自「百萬標記 (Million Marker)」公司的華珍娜 (Jenna Hua) 對此結果表達了挫折感。她質疑道：「我花錢購買，希望能得到好的產品，為什麼卻被欺騙了？」這項研究鑑定出多種危險物質，包括荷爾蒙干擾物與致癌物，也就是已知會導致癌症的物質。其他檢測出的化學物質則與神經系統疾病及生殖系統損害有關。這些物質能透過皮膚被人體吸收，因此它們出現在日常用品中，已成為重大的健康隱憂。

paragraphs.en: One of the most surprising findings was that even products marketed as "natural," "green," or "eco-friendly" were not always safe. The study found that 26% of these products contained at least one dangerous compound, directly contradicting their marketing claims. For example, some items labeled as "100% natural" were found to contain synthetic chemicals, while others labeled as safe included phthalates, which are chemicals often used to make plastics more flexible but are known to be harmful to human health.
paragraphs.zh: 最令人驚訝的發現之一是，即使是行銷標榜為「天然」、「綠色」或「環保」的產品，也未必安全。研究發現，百分之二十六的此類產品至少含有一種危險化合物，這直接與其行銷宣稱相矛盾。例如，有些標示為「百分之百天然」的商品被發現含有合成化學物質，而其他標示為安全的產品則含有鄰苯二甲酸酯，這類化學物質常被用於增加塑膠的柔軟度，但已知對人體健康有害。

paragraphs.en: It remains unclear why these chemicals are present. The authors of the study noted that it is difficult to tell if companies are adding these ingredients on purpose, or if the products are becoming contaminated by accident. Some ingredients may form due to unintended chemical reactions during the manufacturing process. In other cases, chemicals from plastic packaging may leak into the product. Furthermore, the term "fragrance" or "parfum" on a label acts as a catch-all term that can hide up to 1,200 different hazardous chemicals, as companies are not currently required to list them individually.
paragraphs.zh: 目前尚不清楚這些化學物質為何會存在。研究作者指出，很難判斷企業是有意添加這些成分，還是產品在無意間受到污染。有些成分可能是製造過程中發生非預期的化學反應所產生。在其他案例中，塑膠包裝中的化學物質可能會滲入產品。此外，標籤上的「香精」或「香料」一詞是一個概括性術語，可能隱藏了多達一千兩百種有害化學物質，因為目前法規並未要求企業將這些成分逐一列出。

paragraphs.en: This situation creates a difficult environment for smaller businesses that want to do the right thing. According to The Guardian Health, some small producers try to create clean products but are often misled by their own suppliers or unknowingly buy contaminated raw materials. These companies are now worried about facing lawsuits for problems they did not create. Experts suggest that clearer laws and better testing requirements would help these businesses and ensure that all products on the market are safe for the public.
paragraphs.zh: 這種情況為那些想要守法經營的小型企業創造了艱難的環境。根據《衛報健康版》報導，一些小型生產商試圖製造純淨的產品，卻常被供應商誤導，或在不知情下買到受污染的原料。這些公司現在擔心會因非自身造成的過失而面臨訴訟。專家建議，更明確的法律與更完善的檢測要求，將有助於這些企業，並確保市面上所有產品對大眾而言都是安全的。

paragraphs.en: To conduct this research, the team used a method called non-targeted chemical analysis. This allowed them to look for evidence of thousands of different substances rather than just checking for a small list of known chemicals. They identified 303 chemicals that they were confident were present in the products, and they compared these findings against a database of hazardous materials from the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA). The EPA is the government agency responsible for protecting human health and the environment.
paragraphs.zh: 為了進行這項研究，團隊使用了一種稱為「非標靶化學分析」的方法。這讓他們能夠搜尋數千種不同物質的證據，而不僅僅是檢查已知化學物質的清單。他們確認了三百零三種存在於產品中的化學物質，並將這些發現與美國環境保護署 (EPA) 的有害物質資料庫進行比對。環保署是負責保護人類健康與環境的政府機構。

paragraphs.en: Looking ahead, the authors of the study emphasize that the current system of oversight is not enough. They argue that there is an urgent need for mandatory testing to ensure that what is written on a label matches what is actually inside the bottle. As Million Marker continues to raise funds for further testing, the findings serve as a strong reminder for consumers to remain cautious about the products they choose. For now, the study highlights a clear need for stronger regulations to level the playing field and protect consumers from hidden risks in their daily routines.
paragraphs.zh: 展望未來，研究作者強調，目前的監管體系遠遠不足。他們主張，迫切需要強制性檢測，以確保標籤上的內容與瓶子裡的實際成分相符。隨著「百萬標記」持續為後續測試募款，這些發現強烈提醒消費者，對於所選擇的產品應保持謹慎。目前而言，這項研究凸顯了建立更嚴格法規的明確需求，以創造公平的競爭環境，並保護消費者免受日常生活中隱藏風險的危害。

keyTerms.definitionEn: To take further action or get more information about something that has already started.
keyTerms.noteZh: 此片語在文中表示對先前事件的延伸調查。文中：Following up on recent reports about hidden dangers in household items, a new peer-reviewed study has confirmed that many common goods contain toxic chemicals that do not appear on their ingredient labels.

keyTerms.definitionEn: A term or category that includes many different things, often used when there is no specific name for them.
keyTerms.definitionZh: 概括性的、包羅萬象的（術語）。
keyTerms.noteZh: 此詞形容一個詞彙涵蓋了過多且不具體的內容。文中：Furthermore, the term "fragrance" or "parfum" on a label acts as a catch-all term that can hide up to 1,200 different hazardous chemicals, as companies are not currently required to list them individually.

keyTerms.definitionEn: To create a situation where everyone has the same opportunities and advantages.
keyTerms.noteZh: 字面意思是「把球場弄平」，隱喻消除不公平的競爭優勢。文中：For now, the study highlights a clear need for stronger regulations to level the playing field and protect consumers from hidden risks in their daily routines.

previousArticles.title: Hidden Dangers: Study Finds Toxic Chemicals in Everyday Products
previousArticles.summaryEn: A new study has discovered that many personal care products contain toxic chemicals that are not listed on their packaging. Researchers tested over 110 items, including shampoos and baby lotions, and found hidden substances in the vast majority. These chemicals are linked to serious health issues like cancer and reproductive harm. Even products marketed as natural or eco-friendly were found to contain dangerous compounds. The findings have led experts to call for stricter government rules and mandatory safety testing.

quiz.question: According to the study, what is true about products labeled as 'natural' or 'eco-friendly'?

options.A: They are guaranteed to be free of synthetic chemicals.
options.B: More than a quarter of them were found to contain at least one dangerous compound.
options.C: They are safer than standard products because they do not contain phthalates.
options.D: They are strictly regulated by the EPA to ensure the accuracy of their labels.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 B。根據文章第四段，研究發現 26% 標榜「自然」或「環保」的產品含有至少一種危險化合物。選項 A 錯誤，因為文章提到有些標榜 100% 天然的產品仍含有合成化學物質。選項 C 錯誤，因為文章明確指出這些產品中仍可能含有塑化劑（phthalates）。選項 D 錯誤，文章中並未提到 EPA 對這些標籤有特殊的嚴格監管。

quiz.question: What can be inferred about the use of the word 'fragrance' on product labels?

options.A: It is a specific chemical that is generally considered safe for human skin.
options.B: It is a term used by companies to highlight the most expensive ingredients.
options.C: It serves as a legal loophole that allows manufacturers to hide many different chemicals.
options.D: It is the primary reason why small businesses are facing lawsuits from consumers.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 C。根據文章第五段，作者將「fragrance」描述為一個「catch-all term」（概括性術語），允許公司隱藏多達 1,200 種危險化學物質，因為法律不要求個別列出。選項 A 錯誤，因為它是隱藏危險物質的代名詞而非單一安全成分。選項 B 錯誤，它並非用來強調昂貴成分。選項 D 錯誤，雖然小企業面臨訴訟壓力，但文章並未將其歸因於「香精」這單一因素。

quiz.question: In the final paragraph, what does the phrase 'level the playing field' mean?

options.A: To make the competition fair for all businesses by applying the same rules.
options.B: To increase the physical space available for displaying products in retail stores.
options.C: To lower the prices of products so that more people can afford them.
options.D: To remove all government regulations that currently restrict small businesses.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 A。「Level the playing field」是一個慣用語，意指創造公平競爭的環境。在文章脈絡中，這指的是透過更明確的法律與檢測要求，讓誠實的小企業與大公司能在同樣的規範下競爭，避免小企業因供應鏈問題而處於劣勢。選項 B、C、D 皆與該慣用語的商業競爭公平性含義無關。

quiz.question: What is the primary message of the article?

options.A: Consumers should stop using all personal care products immediately.
options.B: Small businesses are solely responsible for the toxic chemicals found in their goods.
options.C: Current regulations are insufficient to protect consumers from hidden toxic chemicals in daily products.
options.D: The EPA has successfully identified all hazardous substances currently sold in major retail stores.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 C。本文的核心在於探討個人護理產品中隱藏的化學風險，並指出目前的監管體系（oversight）不足，呼籲需要更強力的法律與強制檢測來保障消費者權益。選項 A 過於極端，文章建議的是保持謹慎而非全面停用。選項 B 錯誤，文章提到小企業往往是受害者。選項 D 錯誤，文章強調的是現行系統無法有效檢測出這些隱藏的化學物質。
